correctness.rationale: Write W increments D_i independent N(0,1/n). Constraint W_((i+1)/n)−2W_(i/n)+W_((i−1)/n)=0 is exactly D_(i+1)=D_i; Gaussian conditioning at zero projects each independent block onto its constant-increments one-dimensional subspace. Block endpoint sums have independent N(0,length/n) Brownian increments, grid nodes become affine interpolants I_(F_n)B. Original independent fine-grid Brownian bridges survive constraints, with max tail <=2n exp(−2nu²). For any Hausdorff F_n→F, uniform continuity of affine interpolation for continuous f gives I_(F_n)B→I_F B pathwise and bridges vanish, so Q_n weakly converges. Every closed F containing endpoints is grid-approximable. d_H(F_n,[0,1])=δ_n/2 proves sufficiency; macroscopic surviving gap gives a subsequential law with deterministic affine paths on an interval, unlike Wiener, proving necessity. Any nonempty constraint yields finite-n singularity; covariance is Brownian covariance minus independent gap bridge. Independently checked Gaussian Schur complement conditional covariance for every subset of n−1 adjacent second-difference constraints with n=2..6 and continuous midpoint witnesses; finite tests do not replace the tightness/converse proof.
